works.title: Dual Regulation of Monomer Transport Enables Ultrahigh Mg2+/Li+ Selectivity in Polyamide Nanofiltration Membranes
institutions: University of Science and Technology of China
University of Science and Technology of China , , ,
works.abstract: Abstract Nanofiltration membranes are promising for lithium recovery from salt-lake brines, yet their Mg2+/Li+ separation performance can be further improved. Here, we present an organic-phase engineering strategy that systematically tailors the carbon-chain length of alkane solvents, from n-hexane (C6) to 2-methylundecane (C12), to simultaneously regulate piperazine enrichment at the water–organic interface and trimesoyl chloride diffusion kinetics. This dual regulation transforms conventional rapid and random interfacial polymerization into a more confined and homogeneous growth process. The resulting polyamide membranes exhibit a reduced negative surface charge and a narrower and more uniform pore-size distribution. These structural features substantially enhance Mg2+/Li+ separation, with the C12 membrane achieving a Mg2+/Li+ selectivity of up to 306.6 in the mixed-salt solutions. To assess performance under realistic conditions, a two-pass nanofiltration process was evaluated using simulated salt-lake brine. The C12 membrane increased lithium purity from 2.4% to 97.7% while reducing the Mg2+/Li+ mass ratio from 40 to 0.024. This study provides new insight into the kinetic regulation of interfacial polymerization through organic-phase engineering and demonstrates an effective membrane design strategy for high-selectivity lithium extraction from complex brines.

works.abstract: ABSTRACT Manipulating polymer network architecture is critical to advancing organic solvent nanofiltration (OSN) membranes. Here we report a pH‐regulated interfacial polymerization strategy that employs rigid spirobisindane (SBI) monomers bearing hydroxyl and amine functionalities. Regulating phenolic hydroxyl participation enables the same dual‐functional SBI monomer to form either an amide‐dominated or a mixed amide/ester‐linked network, while a hydroxyl‐functional SBI monomer provides an ester‐dominated reference. Spectroscopic characterization, gas sorption analysis, and molecular simulations collectively reveal how network chemistry and packing regulate free‐volume organization and pore‐size distributions, thereby controlling solvent transport and molecular sieving. The mixed amide/ester‐linked SBI‐NH 2 ‐OH membrane exhibits a high microporous surface area (272 m 2 g −1 ) and high methanol permeance (22.7 L m −2 h −1 bar −1 ), whereas the amide‐dominated SBI‐NH 2 membrane provides tight molecular sieving with narrow pore size distributions. In contrast, the ester‐dominated SBI‐OH membrane exhibits larger average interchain spacing and a broader pore‐size distribution, accompanied by reduced selectivity. Notably, the SBI‐derived nanofilms display good pressure stability and solvent resistance. Moreover, successful larger‐area fabrication of both SBI‐NH 2 and SBI‐NH 2 ‐OH membranes demonstrates the compatibility of the fabrication strategy with scale‐up. Taken together, these findings demonstrate pH‐regulated functional‐group participation as a molecular design strategy that translates chemical reactivity into network architecture and transport behavior, offering a rational pathway toward scalable OSN membranes for energy‐efficient separations.

works.abstract: ABSTRACT Biological ion channels achieve multi‐ion discrimination through parallel chemically distinct channel types, each optimized for a single ion species. Replicating this within a single synthetic membrane has remained beyond reach, for conventional membrane resistance blocks the bonding energy difference between different ions. Here we show that an ultrathin polymeric membrane (ca. 8.56 nm) bearing aligned angstrom‐scale porphyrin pores, fabricated by interfacial superspreading, reduces internal resistance sufficiently and achieves simultaneous multi‐ion discrimination. Under a microvolt‐scale applied voltage, the membrane separates six ion species across three valence groups. In particular, the membrane exhibits anomalous selectivity for Li + , with a threshold voltage V t ≈ 400 mV which is 370 mV above the nearest competitor. Applied to lithium extraction from low‐quality brines, a two‐stage device achieves >98% recovery at 1.1 × 10 −4 Wh g −1 (Li) , three orders of magnitude below conventional electrodialysis. This membrane architecture offers a broadly applicable design principle for energy‐intensive separations in which resolving ions of similar charge and size is the critical challenge.

works.title: Aromatic Peptide‐Enabled Cation‐π Engineering in Lamellar Nanochannels for Enhanced Cation Selectivity
institutions: Qingdao University
Shandong University of Technology
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Ion selectivity is central to nanochannel membranes for ion separation, molecular recognition, and energy conversion. However, conventional membranes primarily rely on electrostatic repulsion to regulate ion selectivity; the short‐range and weak nature limits high selectivity. Herein, a cation‐π engineering strategy is proposed by intercalating aromatic peptides (APs) into sub‐nanometer graphene oxide (GO) channels. Systematic tuning of the π‐system with phenylalanine (F)‐, tyrosine (Y)‐, and tryptophan (W)‐based peptides reveals a dual role of cation‐π interactions, involving electrostatic attraction and cation confinement. Specifically, the Y‐based AP‐intercalated GO membrane achieves a cation transference number of 0.614, representing a 16.95% improvement over GO membrane, which is attributed to electrostatic attraction of π‐system toward cations. Significantly, experiments and simulations reveal a nonmonotonic relation between selectivity and π‐system density, excessive π‐system density strengthens confinement and compromises selectivity. Moreover, the W‐based AP‐intercalated GO membrane exhibits a maximum power density of 20.11 W/m 2 under a 50‐fold NaCl gradient through an optimized selectivity‐permeability balance. Notably, the power density is increased to 29.99 W/m 2 after introducing Mg 2+ , which competitively occupies indole π‐sites to facilitate Na + transport. This work uncovers the role of cation‐π interactions in confined channels, offering a chemical design principle for selective ion‐channel membranes.

works.title: Insights into Desalination Performance of Spacing-Tunable Laminated MXene Membranes via Molecular Dynamics and Machine Learning
institutions: Hangzhou Dianzi University
Hangzhou Dianzi University , , ,
works.abstract: Abstract Developing desalination membranes that combine high water permeance with high ion rejection remains important for freshwater production. Laminated MXene membranes are promising because their surface chemistry and channel dimensions are tunable, yet the respective roles of sheet-edge openings and interlayer spacing in staggered channels remain unclear. We performed molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of 242 O- and F-terminated Ti3C2 MXene membrane systems, varying the sheet-edge gap and interlayer spacing, d, from 6 to 16 Å. Machine learning (ML) analysis identified gap as the main structural variable governing water permeance and the extent of ion penetration, while d further regulated transport within the interlayer channels. Water and ion density distributions showed that gap primarily controlled entry into the laminated membrane, whereas d affected postentry transport and ion hydration. Na–Ow radial distribution functions and hydration-loss analyses indicated that narrow interlayer channels mainly perturbed the second hydration shell of Na+. Under matched geometries, surface termination produced weaker and more localized changes in water and ion distributions. These results distinguish entry control by the sheet-edge gap from postentry regulation by interlayer spacing and provide molecular guidance for designing spacing-tunable laminated MXene membranes.

works.title: Divalent Cations and Chlorine Synergistically Reshape T6SS-Mediated Microbial Competition in Water Distribution System Biofilms
institutions: Shanghai Jiao Tong University
works.abstract: Abstract Microbial interactions shape the community structure and function in drinking water distribution system (DWDS) biofilms, yet how the dynamic competition is regulated in biofilms remains poorly understood. Here, we show that divalent cations (Ca2+, Mg2+) and chlorine in drinking water synergistically activate the type VI secretion system (T6SS) in opportunistic pathogens within biofilms. Field-collected biofilms serve as ecological hotspots that selectively enrich specific T6SS-harboring pathogens. Using simulated pipe systems and mutant validation, we further establish that divalent cations and chlorine enhance c-di-GMP signaling to promote T6SS-mediated colonization. This activation stimulates EPS production, whose polysaccharides mitigate T6SS attack, dampening the competitive advantage during mid-stage maturation but allowing gradual resurgence over extended succession. This divalent cation-chlorine-driven interplay shapes ecological succession, selectively retaining T6SS-proficient cells and establishing a “biofilm reservoir effect.” Under chlorine decay, T6SS-active pathogens can be released into bulk water, elevating exposure risks. Conversely, reducing divalent cations via nanofiltration suppresses T6SS across multiple pathogens, limiting reservoir accumulation and release. Our findings identify divalent cation availability as a key environmental signal associated with T6SS-mediated competition, linking water chemistry to pathogen persistence. This work suggests integrating membrane-based divalent cation removal with chlorine management as a chemistry-based strategy to mitigate microbial risks, advancing an integrated water quality paradigm for drinking water safety.

works.title: Coverage-Aware Break-Even Conditions for Polymeric Membrane-Based Water Reuse in Arid Urban Systems
institutions: AI Center, Faculty of Computer and Information Systems, Islamic University of Madinah, Madinah 42351, Saudi Arabia
Department of Civil Engineering, Prince Sattam Bin Abdulaziz University, Al-Kharj 11942, Saudi Arabia
AI V&V Lab, King Fahd University of Petroleum and Minerals, Dhahran 31261, Saudi Arabia
Civil Engineering Department, Faculty of Engineering, Islamic University of Madinah, Madinah 42351, Saudi Arabia
works.abstract: A utility reclaiming effluent with polymeric membranes must choose a configuration and a deployment coverage. A coverage-aware volume and cost model for an illustrative arid zone of 10Mm3/yr compares ultrafiltration (Configuration A) with ultrafiltration plus polyamide thin-film-composite reverse osmosis (Configuration B). Membrane parameters are literature-derived, eligibility and placement assumed, and no experiments were performed. At 50% coverage and 1 USD/m3, Configuration A avoids 11.5 percentage points of potable input at 0.48 USD/m3 and Configuration B 20.4 points at 0.70 USD/m3, or 0.56 and 0.82 USD/m3 without real-loss credit. Break-even coverages are 11.7% and 11.5%. Configuration B is preferable above a crossover value of 0.98 USD/m3 (1.15 without loss credit) and leads in 46.2% of paired draws at 1 USD/m3. Feed salinity, regulation, concentrate cost, and capital and financing costs move the crossover most. Under independent inputs and assumed eligibility, approved demand rather than recovery limits volume in at least 98.8% of draws, and placement dominates net-benefit variance. Adverse feed conditions that couple operating and cost parameters make treatment costs comparably influential for Configuration B. The thresholds are conditional criteria, not city-specific predictions.

works.title: Slippery Amphiphilic Antifouling Loose Nanofiltration Membrane with “Double-Defense” Functionalities for High-Salinity Organic Wastewater Sustainable Management
institutions: Sun Yat-sen University
Guangdong Provincial Key Laboratory of Environmental Pollution Control and Remediation Technology
Sun Yat-Sen University , , ,
Guangdong Provincial Key Laboratory of Environmental Pollution Control and Remediation Technology , ,
works.abstract: Abstract Loose nanofiltration (LNF) holds potential for sustainable management of high-salinity organic wastewater through precise organics/salts fractionation, but practical application is constrained by severe organic–inorganic combined fouling. Herein, we propose a “double-defense” antifouling strategy and develop a slippery amphiphilic LNF membrane via facile stepwise surface modification. A hydrophilic branched polyethylenimine (PEI) network was first cross-linked onto a polyamide (PA) substrate to form a fouling-resistant protection layer, followed by covalent grafting of liquid-like polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) brushes to confer a slippery, fouling-release surface. The PEI layer acts as a hydration and electrostatic barrier to repel organic-cation complexes and scale precursors, while the slippery PDMS layer with high mobility and low surface energy minimizes interfacial interactions and strengthens hydraulic shear responsiveness. During the concentration of authentic leachate membrane bioreactor (MBR) effluent, the optimized membrane showed superior antifouling performance: low flux decline ratio (FDR) of 41.6% and high flux recovery ratio (FRR) of 98.1%, outperforming a commercial PA membrane (FDR 91.2%, FRR 78.4%). It also delivered an organics/salts fractionation selectivity 7.8 times that of the commercial membrane, demonstrating multiple cycles stability. This rationally designed architecture offers a practical solution for challenging wastewater and is extensible to other PA-based membrane systems in environmental applications.

works.title: Voltage Gated Ion Entry Into Two‐dimensional Angstrom‐Scale Channels
institutions: Department of Physics & Astronomy, School of Natural Sciences University of Manchester Manchester UK
National Graphene Institute The University of Manchester Manchester UK
Department of Chemistry, School of Natural Sciences The University of Manchester Manchester UK

Department of Physics Indian Institute of Technology Gandhinagar Gujarat India
Photon Science Institute The University of Manchester Manchester UK
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Biological ion channels with angstrom‐scale (Å‐scale) constrictions regulate key physiological processes by controlling ion flow via stimuli such as voltage gating across cellular membranes. Artificial Å‐scale channels can reveal insights into the voltage‐gating mechanisms, especially the role of geometrical constrictions on ion entry and dehydration. Here, we investigate voltage‐gating in artificial slit‐shaped channels with a height ( h ) of one monolayer of graphene, fabricated from layered materials. In the resting state, these channels exhibit selective ion exclusion while permitting flow for water molecules. Under the influence of high voltage, we observe a transition from an insulating to a highly conducting state, facilitating ion permeation beyond a threshold voltage. Our experimental findings unveil non‐linear hysteretic current‐voltage ( I–V ) characteristics, which we attribute to a confinement‐induced ion‐entry energy barrier involving ion dehydration and electrostatic effects. The applied voltage can facilitate ion entry by modifying this barrier, potentially through partial dehydration or rearrangement of the hydration shell. Molecular simulations further reveal distinct ion concentrations and mobilities inside the channel during forward and reverse voltage sweeps, demonstrating the influence of the structural organization of confined water on ion transport.

works.title: Surface‐Coordinated Gas–Solid Polymerization Enables Quasi‐2D Polyphenylacetylene Single‐Crystalline Nanoribbons
institutions: State Key Laboratory of Functional Crystals and Devices Fujian Institute of Research on the Structure of Matter Chinese Academy of Sciences Fuzhou Fujian P. R. China
Fujian Science & Technology Innovation Laboratory for Optoelectronic Information of China Fuzhou Fujian P. R. China
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Two‐dimensional (2D) conjugated polymer single crystals are highly desirable for optoelectronics, yet their realization is limited by the intrinsic coupling between molecular‐weight buildup and chain entanglement, which disrupts long‐range order. Here, we report a gas–solid interfacial polymerization strategy that decouples monomer diffusion from chain propagation, enabling the growth of quasi‐2D polyphenylacetylene (PPA) single‐crystalline nanoribbons on Cu/CuO x surfaces. This process is likely enabled by surface coordination‐assisted activation of phenylacetylene and directional π‐stacking‐driven assembly, which suppress chain entanglement and promote crystallographic ordering. As a result, micrometer‐scale PPA single‐crystalline nanoribbons with left‐handed cis‐transoidal helical chains and long‐range crystallinity are obtained. Under an ideal fully extended‐chain model, the PPA chains exhibit a geometrically estimated upper‐bound molecular weight of up to ∼3.7 × 10 9 g mol − 1 . The resulting PPA nanoribbons exhibit efficient charge transport and broadband photodetection from 375 to 1550 nm, with a responsivity of 30.1 A W − 1 and a detectivity of 8.65 × 10 1 2 Jones. This interfacial synthesis strategy provides a route to overcoming the trade‐off between molecular‐weight buildup and structural order in conjugated polymers, offering opportunities for quasi‐2D polymer semiconductors in flexible optoelectronics and programmable chiral materials.

works.title: Casting-Derived PVA/PDMS Janus Membranes with Stable Photothermal Conversion for Solar Desalination
institutions: Seoul National University , , ,
Seoul National University College of Medicine , , ,
Advanced Institutes of Convergence Technology , , ,
Seoul National University , , , ,
FineNano Ltd. , Rm. 1027, 10F, Ace Smartwing Yeongtong, 253 Samsung-ro , Yeongtong-gu, , ,
works.abstract: Abstract Solar photothermal conversion enables water evaporation and purification through localized interfacial heating, offering a sustainable approach for solar energy utilization. However, integrating efficient solar harvesting, continuous water transport, and structural support within a simply fabricated membrane remains challenging. In this study, a casting-derived Janus bilayer photothermal membrane was developed by integrating a hydrophilic PVA/FeCo@C/CNTs/ACNTs photothermal layer with a hydrophobic PDMS/ZnO nanorod supporting layer. The multicomponent FeCo@C/CNTs/ACNTs photothermal layer provides strong broadband solar absorption and efficient photothermal conversion, while the PVA matrix facilitates continuous water transport through swelling-assisted hydration. Meanwhile, the PDMS/ZnO nanorod layer provides mechanical support for the PVA-based photothermal layer and contributes to the structural integrity of the bilayer membrane during interfacial evaporation. Under 1.5 sun irradiation, the membrane surface temperature reached 83.7 °C, while an evaporation rate of 1.618 kg·m–2·h–1 was achieved under 1 sun irradiation. In addition, the membrane demonstrated effective performance in solar-driven seawater desalination and dye-containing water purification, highlighting its potential for solar-driven water-treatment applications.

works.title: Molecular design of ion-selective polymer membranes for electrochemical water purification and resource recovery
institutions: Clarkson University
Central Electrochemical Research Institute
Academy of Scientific and Innovative Research
works.abstract: Ion-selective membranes enable electrochemical water purification and resource recovery. Effective molecular design must balance preferential target-ion uptake, rapid transport, and limited water crossover under changing feed and electrical conditions. This review examines how fixed charge, hydration, pathway connectivity, and ion-specific interactions govern transport in charged polymers, microporous materials, recognition membranes, selective surface layers, and covalent organic frameworks. Hydration reshapes transport pathways, making their hydrated dimensions and connectivity more informative than dry pore size alone. Strong binding can favor uptake while slowing release and passage, so selective uptake need not yield selective flux. Designs that partly decouple charge density from swelling or binding affinity from mobility offer ways to balance discrimination and throughput. Practical deployment requires reproducible selectivity, resistance, and water-transport properties across large-scale membrane production. Transport-state retention then requires maintaining these properties as polymer chemistry, hydration, and interfaces evolve during operation. Evaluating them together connects molecular design, manufacturing quality, and durability to current efficiency, product purity, concentration, recovery, and energy consumption in complex feeds.

works.title: Theoretical Calculations of CO2/CH4 Separation through Windowed Carbon Nanotube Membranes
institutions: Sichuan Police College
Sichuan Police College , , ,
works.abstract: Abstract Distinct topological features endow windowed carbon nanotube (CNT) membranes with great potential as molecular sieves for efficient gas separation and purification. In this work, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations were adopted to systematically investigate the CO2/CH4 selective separation performance of such membranes. Key structural and operational parameters, including CNT diameter, pressure, initial feed gas molar ratio, and nanowindow density, were modulated to comprehensively evaluate the molecular sieving capacity toward CO2 and CH4. Simulation results reveal that heteroatom-functionalized windowed CNT membranes exhibit outstanding CO2 permselectivity and superior CH4 purification capacity, with a maximum CO2/CH4 separation selectivity of 41. Among all simulated configurations, the 4N5F-modified nanowindow CNT membrane exhibits the optimal separation performance, yielding a CO2 capture fraction of 0.77 and recovered CH4 purity of 97.6%. Such excellent molecular sieving performance confirms that windowed CNT membranes hold promising prospects for direct CO2 capture and raw shale gas purification.

works.title: An integrated pervaporation-dia-nanofiltration process for aroma recovery and ethanol removal in white wine
works.abstract: Membrane technologies are widely used in ethanol removal from wine (DW); however, they face challenges in maintaining wine quality, particularly in retaining volatile compounds. This study evaluated for the first time a two-stage membrane process (PV-NF) combining pervaporation (PV) and dia-nanofiltration (dia-NF) to produce a white dealcoholized wine-based beverages (DW; ethanol <0.5% v /v) with aroma preservation. PV was first used to extract and recover aroma compounds from the original wine (OW). The resulting dearomatized wine underwent dia-NF for ethanol removal, after which the recovered aroma concentrate was reconstituted into the final DW, ensuring its alcohol content did not exceed 0.5% v /v. Additionally, the physicochemical, color, and volatile profiles of the produced DWs were studied. The results indicated that total acidity and volatile acidity were reduced by 80–82% and 35–52%, respectively. Furthermore, reducing sugars, glycerin, malic acid, and tartaric acid experienced partial depletion, while citric acid was completely lost. Color profiles were also impacted; the extended processing time of the combined PV-NF approach, elevating the browning index (Abs 420 nm) to as high as 0.71 AU compared to the OW (0.07 AU). The PV-NF process successfully produced DW with ethanol content below 0.5% v /v while retaining 27–31% of total aroma compounds, outperforming NF alone (6–9% retention). These findings highlight the potential of combining PV-NF to mitigate volatile losses during the process and stress the need for optimizing processing strategies to balance ethanol reduction with sensory integrity.

works.abstract: Abstract Achieving high room-temperature ionic conductivity without sacrificing mechanical and thermal stability remains a central challenge for polyamide-based ion-solvating membranes (ISMs). Herein, we develop a rigid−flexible coordination strategy by incorporating controlled amounts of flexible aromatic ether linkages into a rigid fluorinated aromatic polyamide backbone. The amide-rich aromatic framework provides mechanical and thermal robustness, whereas the ether-containing segments regulate chain packing, Lewis-basic coordination-site density, and LiTFSI dissociation. Systematic comparison of PA-TFDB, PA-6FODA, and PA-6FAPB demonstrates that Li+ transport does not increase monotonically with ether content but instead reaches a maximum at an intermediate rigid−flexible balance. The optimized PA-6FODA-40-ISM exhibits an ionic conductivity of 9.18 × 10−4 S cm−1, representing a 2.4-fold enhancement over PA-TFDB-40-ISM, together with a Li+ transference number of 0.72, an apparent migration activation energy of 0.0402 eV, and oxidative stability up to 4.95 V. Raman analysis reveals a free-TFSI– fraction of 64% in PA-6FODA-40-ISM, compared with 46% in PA-6FAPB-40-ISM and 37% in PA-TFDB-40-ISM. Combined X-ray diffraction, spectroscopic, and density functional theory analyses indicate that the balanced rigid−flexible architecture produces less organized chain packing and a heterogeneous Li+-binding-energy landscape, thereby promoting salt dissociation and facilitating Li+ exchange between polymer and solvent coordination environments. In contrast, insufficient ether coordination favors contact ion pairs, whereas excessive ether-site density is accompanied by stronger coordination and increased ion aggregation. PA-6FODA-40-ISM simultaneously retains a tensile strength of 43 MPa, an elongation at break of 112%, and dimensional stability at 160 °C. The Li∣PA-6FODA-40-ISM∣Li symmetric cell maintained stable cycling for 250 h at 0.1 mA cm−2 and 0.1 mAh cm−2, while LFP∥Li cells retain 83% of their initial capacity after 300 cycles at 0.5 C. These findings establish rigid−flexible coordination as an effective molecular design principle for balancing ion transport, structural robustness, and interfacial stability in aromatic polyamide ISMs.

works.title: The Nexus Between Heat and Vacuum Pumps: A Novel Hybrid Desalination System
institutions: Department of Industrial Thermal Power Engineering, South Ural State University (National Research University), 454080 Chelyabinsk, Russia
Department of Electric Power Generation Stations, Network and Supply-Systems, South Ural State University (National Research University), 454080 Chelyabinsk, Russia
works.abstract: The thermal vacuum distillation of seawater, preheated by a hybrid solar heat pump, is a candidate technology for autonomous and hot-climate sites, but experimental energy and exergy data for it are scarce. The objective of this study is to determine the energy and exergy characteristics of a laboratory vacuum distiller and to describe them with a semi-empirical model whose validity limits are stated explicitly. A 5 L batch distiller was tested at four temperature/pressure regimes (75 °C/0.4 atm, 85 °C/0.6 atm, 90 °C/0.7 atm and 100 °C/1 atm). The model combines empirical correlations for heating and maintenance energies with an evaporation fraction; this is calibrated on the four regimes and restricted to physically admissible conditions. The productivity increased from 125 to 334 g/h, and the specific energy consumption was 3.8–5.7 Wh/g. The vacuum regime had the highest specific energy consumption (5.7 Wh/g against 3.8–4.1 Wh/g at 85–100 °C), so no energy advantage of vacuum operation was demonstrated. The calibrated model reproduced measured productivity and total energy values within 2.7% and 4.5%, respectively; leave-one-out cross-validation gave errors up to 94%, so the predictive capability of the model is limited and the model should be regarded as a descriptive fit of the four measured regimes. The eight model parameters were fitted to twelve measured values, and no independent validation data were available. The effect of pressure cannot be separated from that of temperature, because the two variables increase together (correlation coefficient, 0.99). The exergy efficiency was 1.6–3.2%: 93.8–95.8% of the fuel exergy was destroyed by irreversibilities and 2.6–3.1% was lost with the residual hot water; 41–44% of the exergy destruction occurred in the heating stage. Relative to the minimum work of separation, the second-law efficiency was only 0.014–0.020%. The measured energy inputs exclude the heat pump and the photovoltaic–thermal panel; therefore, the benefit of renewable-energy integration is prospective and was not quantified. Scientific novelty: This study conducts a combined experimental, semi-empirical and exergy assessment of the thermal vacuum distillation of seawater preheated by a hybrid solar-powered heat pump, with explicitly defined model validity limits. Practical contribution: This study presents laboratory-scale reference values of the specific energy consumption and exergy efficiency of the model, and identifies the main loss sources for the design of an industrial prototype. The delivery of distilled water to remote areas by unmanned aerial vehicles is considered only as a prospective application and was not studied.

works.title: 3D Solar‐Driven Interfacial Evaporator Based on Tailored TiO <sub>2</sub> Nanotube Arrays by Wireless Anodizing for Efficient Desalination
institutions: Shanghai Maritime University
Shanghai Ship and Shipping Research Institute
College of Ocean Science and Engineering Shanghai Maritime University Shanghai People's Republic of China
Merchant Marine College Shanghai Maritime University Shanghai People's Republic of China
Shanghai Ship and Shipping Research Institute Co., LTD. Shanghai People's Republic of China
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Solar‐driven interfacial evaporation is an energy‐efficient desalination strategy. However, the existing solar‐driven interfacial evaporators mostly rely on a surface‐localized photothermal layer for heat confinement, which limits evaporation exclusively to the top surface. The internal transfer channels and potential evaporation area remain unexplored, restricting water production rates. Here, a wireless anodization with a composite bipolar electrode has been proposed to prepare completely internal anodized porous Ti with TiO 2 nanotube (TNT) arrays, serving for 3D solar‐driven interfacial evaporation. By regulating the reaction area and intensity, the TiO 2 nanotubes (TNTs) with tailored size (diameter of 120–170 nm, length of 3–10 µm) have successfully anisotropically grown on the porous Ti substrates, constructing internal interconnected channels. The obtained wireless anodized porous Ti (WAPT) possessed an increased surface area of 7.938 m 2 ·g −1 , as well as solar absorbance >80%, superhydrophilicity (totally wetting within 10 s), and low evaporation enthalpy (451.83 kJ·kg −1 ), making efficient water evaporation with larger evaporation area and lower energy consumption possible. Under one‐sun irradiation, the WAPT showed an evaporation rate of 1.68 kg·m −2 ·h −1 with no salt crystallization and could maintain over 30 days. By assembling the WAPTs into a 3D interfacial evaporator, cooperated with wind‐driven cold evaporation, the maximum evaporation rate reached 2.412 kg·m −2 ·h −1 . In outdoor conditions (solar intensity of 0.6 kW·m −2 at 12 pm), the water collection rate reached 1.59 kg·m −2 ·h −1 . This work should make possible the development of a high‐performance solar‐driven interfacial evaporator for various applications.

works.title: Buried Reed Barrier Layers for Sustainable Desalination of Coastal Saline Soils
institutions: College of Water Conservancy and Civil Engineering, Shandong Agricultural University, Tai’an 271018, China
works.abstract: Soil salinization poses severe threats to agricultural production and ecological sustainability in the Yellow River Delta of China. Conventional porous barrier materials such as straw, river sand and construction waste have unavoidable limitations in raw-material supply and environmental safety. This study explored the potential of Phragmites australis segments as an eco-friendly, locally available porous barrier layer for sustainable coastal saline-soil remediation. Laboratory soil column simulation tests were carried out with four reed-segment length treatments (2 cm, 5 cm, 8 cm, 11 cm) and a reed-free control (CK) to investigate soil percolation and drainage, vertical salt content distribution and layered desalination rate. Buried reed segments significantly enhanced percolation and drainage under leaching, with the 5 cm treatment performing best. After leaching, soil salt content increased monotonically with depth in all treatments, and CK retained significantly higher salt contents than the reed-amended treatments throughout the profile. Reed-segment length exerted slight effects on topsoil desalination but significant effects on deep soil layers. All reed treatments achieved higher desalination rates than CK. The 5 cm treatment yielded stable salt-mass-weighted profile desalination rates of 96.59%, 96.76% and 97.15% at 24 h, 84 h and 168 h, respectively, showing optimal performance under laboratory soil-column conditions. These findings provide a sustainable, low-cost technical reference for the ecological amelioration of coastal saline soils.

works.title: Ligand-engineered layered solid–liquid interfaces enable fast and selective ion transport
works.abstract: Abstract Ion transport behaviors are central to ion separation, micro-/nano-fluidics, and interfacial catalysis, yet achieving high ion transport rate and selectivity remains challenging in nonaqueous systems. Here, we propose a unique solid–liquid cooperative interface built from a layered cyano-bridged metal framework (CMF) and nonaqueous solvents to simultaneously increase cation (Li+) conductivity (9.5 mS·cm−1) and transport selectivity (~ 0.9). Mechanistic analysis based on theoretical calculations, supported by electrochemical measurements, shows that the nonaqueous solvents can work as functional interfacial ligands at the surface of layered CMFs, including outer-layer solvent ligands (OSLs) and interlayer solvent ligands (ISLs), which can restructure the interfacial Li+ migration environment and salt speciation. It is found that OSLs with higher polarity symmetry would interact more strongly with the unsaturated metal sites on the CMF’s surface, thereby promoting coordination competition at the interface, accelerating solvation-renewal dynamics, and increasing the Li+ transport rate. ISLs with higher polarity symmetry could stabilize a low-curvature surface of CMF, strengthen anion anchoring at the unsaturated metal sites, increase selectivity for Li+ transport, and further improve overall Li+ transport rate. Therefore, we provide a potential strategy to construct a unique solid–liquid interface using CMF solids and rationally designed interfacial solvent ligands to promote the ion transport behaviors.

works.title: 3D-Printed Photocatalytic Spacers for Fouling Control and Pollutant Degradation in Membrane Water Treatment: Design Strategies and Prospects for Electrodialysis and Nanofiltration
institutions: Lund University
University of Ghana
Division of Chemical Engineering, Department of Process and Life Science Engineering, Lund University, Naturvetarvägen 14, 221 00 Lund, Sweden
Department of Materials Science and Engineering, School of Engineering Sciences, University of Ghana, Accra, P.O. Box LG 77, Ghana
works.abstract: Feed spacers are indispensable components of aqueous membrane processes, but conventional fabrication methods such as extrusion and injection moulding constrain spacer geometry to simple net-type designs, limiting further gains in mass transfer and fouling control. Additive manufacturing (3D-printing) has relaxed these geometric constraints and, more recently, enabled the integration of photocatalytic functionality directly onto the spacer structure, allowing a single component to simultaneously provide mechanical support, hydrodynamic mixing, and in situ pollutant degradation. This review describes the fundamentals of spacer hydrodynamics, including the roles of filament diameter, mesh angle, porosity, and channel height in governing concentration and temperature polarization before surveying the photocatalytic materials, such as TiO2, g-C3N4, iron oxides/oxyhydroxides, metal-organic frameworks and conducting polymers, and synthesis routes (hydrothermal, sol-gel/dip-coating, in situ polymerization, microwave-assisted) used to functionalize 3D-printed spacers. NF and ED are selected as the two spacer-dependent processes most widely used in water treatment and are discussed separately because of their different driving forces. Design strategies for integrating photocatalysts onto printed spacer architecture, the resulting fouling-control mechanisms, and reported performance in electrodialysis and nanofiltration systems are critically assessed, alongside emerging cross-cutting applications. Because direct data on photocatalytic spacers in NF and ED are still scarce, results obtained with spacers are distinguished from extrapolations from photocatalytic membrane studies. Key challenges, specifically photocatalyst loading stability under prolonged operation and light delivery within enclosed membrane modules, are identified among the principal barriers to scale-up, while 4D-printed stimulus responsive spacers, machine-learning-guided geometry optimization, and photothermal-photocatalytic coupling are highlighted as promising future directions. Furthermore, 3D-printed photocatalytic spacers represent a convergent technology capable of simultaneously addressing concentration polarization, organic fouling, biofouling, and micropollutant degradation within a single structural component. Three-dimensional-printed photocatalytic spacers may contribute to the mitigation of concentration polarization, organic fouling, biofouling, and micropollutant degradation within a single component, although these phenomena are governed by different mechanisms and their simultaneous control involves design trade-offs.

works.title: Seawater Desalination in the Middle East and North Africa: Environmental Impacts of Brine Discharge, Energy Use and Pathways to Sustainable Expansion in Egypt
works.abstract: Desalination has become indispensable to water security in the Middle East and North Africa (MENA), which produces almost half of the world's desalinated water. Egypt, facing a widening gap between Nile supply and demand, plans to expand seawater desalination from about 1.2–1.4 million m³ per day today to several million m³ per day within a decade. This review synthesises evidence on the environmental impacts of desalination, with emphasis on brine discharge, chemical additives, intake effects and energy use, and on management options relevant to Egypt's Mediterranean and Red Sea coasts. Globally, about 15,900 plants produce some 95 million m³ per day of fresh water and about 142 million m³ per day of brine, of which about 70% is produced in MENA. Brine, typically with roughly twice the salinity of seawater and containing antiscalants, coagulants and cleaning chemicals, can form dense plumes that affect seagrasses, corals and benthic communities near outfalls, particularly in poorly flushed embayments. Intakes cause impingement and entrainment of marine organisms, and energy use, still dominated by fossil fuels, generates substantial greenhouse-gas emissions. The review shows that most impacts can be reduced through careful site selection, subsurface intakes, diffuser outfalls, environmental monitoring, renewable energy and emerging brine-valorisation technologies, and proposes guidelines for Egypt's expansion, particularly to protect the Red Sea's coral reefs.

works.title: Boronic acid-functionalized graphene aerogels for selective catechol removal in complex multicomponent phenolic aerosols
institutions: China Tobacco
China Tobacco Yunnan Industrial Co., Ltd. (China)
Zhejiang University
Kunming University of Science and Technology
Linyi University
works.abstract: Selective adsorption in complex multicomponent aerosols remains challenging because structurally similar molecules often compete for identical adsorption sites. Herein, a boronic acid-functionalized three-dimensional graphene aerogel was developed as a selective adsorbent for phenolic compounds. Following 1,2-benzenediboronic acid modification, the specific surface area of graphene aerogel increased from 380.69 to 539.88 m 2 g −1 . In dynamic multicomponent aerosol experiments, the detected catechol amounts after filtration through B-14/CA and B-18/CA were 65.94 and 65.21 μg/cig, respectively, compared with 106.13 μg/cig for the conventional cellulose acetate filter. Other representative phenolic compounds exhibited responses distinct from that of catechol, demonstrating differential filtration in the competitive system. Density functional theory calculations showed that the optimized catechol complex did not correspond to a conventional boronate ester. Instead, a noncovalent B···O contact of approximately 2.06 Å closed a seven-membered pseudo-cyclic adsorption configuration without dehydration. The similar adsorption energies of catechol and guaiacol, −0.34319 and −0.34799 eV, respectively, indicated that a single optimized adsorption energy was insufficient to explain the experimental difference. These results suggest that the combination of hierarchical porous transport and configuration-dependent noncovalent recognition contributes to preferential catechol retention in multicomponent aerosols.

works.title: Probing Adsorbed Water in Al(HCOO)3 Metal–Organic Framework by Multinuclear and Multidimensional Solid-State NMR Spectroscopy
institutions: Center of High Field NMR Spectroscopy and Imaging, Nanyang Technological University, 21 Nanyang Link, Singapore 637371, Singapore
Tianjin Key Lab for Rare Earth Materials and Applications, School of Materials Science and Engineering, Nankai University, Tianjin 300350, China
works.abstract: Water affects the local structure, dynamics, and adsorption properties of metal–organic frameworks (MOFs), yet the molecular-level characterization of confined water remains difficult due to the lack of long-range ordering. Here, we study the water adsorption in microporous MOF Al(HCOO)3 using multinuclear solid-state NMR spectroscopy combined with ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) simulations. 1H NMR resolves two distinct confined-water environments and reveals water–framework and water–water contacts. 13C and 27Al NMR further show that water adsorption perturbs the local environments of the formate linkers and AlO6 coordination units. Powder X-ray diffraction shows that the long-range crystalline framework is preserved after water loading, whereas 13C NMR detects a minor mobile formate-containing species that disappears upon re-dehydration, consistent with the partial local hydrolysis of the framework. 2H NMR distinguishes both highly mobile and confined water undergoing rapid anisotropic reorientation. The effective quadrupolar line shape is consistent with rapid anisotropic reorientation, for which C2-axis flips provide one possible motional model. 1H–2H CP-HETCOR NMR further suggests dipolar contacts between restricted water molecules, the formate framework, and neighboring water molecules. AIMD simulations support water–framework interactions associated with the two pore environments and the formation of an interconnected water network. These results provide molecular-level insights into the water adsorption sites and dynamics in Al(HCOO)3 and the previously unreported partial hydrolysis of this MOF.
